modules.description: Build hygienic habits from entry into the production area through task changes, and prevent cross-contamination by separating zones, equipment, and material flows.

lessons.caution: Do not enter a food-handling area with symptoms or an unreported wound.

checks.explanation: Symptoms, wounds, clothing, and hair can be sources of contamination; report any problem before starting work.
options: To prevent worker-borne contamination from reaching the product
So production records do not need to be made
To replace temperature checks of ingredients
So workers can bypass zone rules
checks.prompt: Why are health and clothing checks done before handling food?

checks.explanation: Gloves do not eliminate the risk of illness. Report the symptoms and wait for work instructions.
options: Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Move the product to another group to meet the target
Report the symptoms to the supervisor and do not handle food; wait for a safe work assignment according to facility procedure.
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: Before the shift starts, a worker has diarrhea and plans to wear gloves to package ready-to-eat products. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Read the entry rules for the production zone → Check your physical condition and report symptoms or wounds → Wear clothing and hair covering as required → Request a recheck before handling food.
options: Read the entry rules for the production zone
Wear clothing and hair covering as required
Check your physical condition and report symptoms or wounds
Request a recheck before handling food
checks.prompt: In the workflow “Health check and entry to the production area,” what should you do after completing the first step?

dialogue.japanese: 少し熱があります。責任者に報告します。
dialogue.meaning: I have a slight fever. I will report it to the person in charge.
dialogue.reading: すこしねつがあります。せきにんしゃにほうこくします。

dialogue.japanese: 作業を始める前に、体調を確認してください。
dialogue.meaning: Before starting work, check your health.
dialogue.reading: さぎょうをはじめるまえに、たいちょうをかくにんしてください。

objectives: Memeriksa kondisi tubuh, pakaian kerja, rambut, dan perlengkapan sebelum menangani pangan.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Report the symptoms to the leader and do not handle food; wait to be assigned safe duties under facility procedures.
lessons.scenario: Before the shift begins, a worker has diarrhea and plans to wear gloves while packaging ready-to-eat product.

sections.body: Workers can carry contaminants on their hands, hair, clothing, or wounds. An entry check can identify fever, diarrhea, vomiting, wounds, or dirty clothing before products are exposed. Follow the facility's hygiene plan: report the issue, and let the person in charge assign safe duties.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before entering, read the posted instructions, store personal items, change clothing according to the zone, cover your hair, and check your equipment. If you feel unwell or a wound dressing comes loose, stop tasks involving food and tell the leader. Do not hide a health problem to meet production targets.

Practice scenario: Before the shift begins, a worker has diarrhea and plans to wear gloves while packaging ready-to-eat product.
Suggested response: Report the symptoms to the leader and do not handle food; wait to be assigned safe duties under facility procedures.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Baca aturan masuk untuk zona produksi
Periksa kondisi tubuh dan laporkan gejala atau luka
Kenakan pakaian dan penutup rambut sesuai aturan
Minta pemeriksaan ulang sebelum mulai menangani pangan
lessons.title: Health Checks and Entry to the Production Area

lessons.caution: Do not keep using the same gloves after touching waste, a phone, or raw ingredients.

checks.explanation: Dirty hands can contaminate new gloves when putting them on; wash your hands first.
options: Wash your hands according to procedure first
Just spray the outside of the old gloves
Rinse the food that was touched
Put on two pairs of gloves without washing your hands
checks.prompt: What should you do before putting on new gloves after touching a waste bin?

checks.explanation: The gloves have touched waste; stop contact with the product, discard the gloves, wash your hands, and put on new ones.
options: Do not continue filling. Discard the gloves, wash your hands according to procedure, and put on new gloves before returning to the product.
Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Move the product to another group to meet the target
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: A worker touches a waste-bin handle with gloves, then is about to fill a ready-to-eat product container. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Stop contact with the product and discard the soiled gloves → Wash your hands in the posted sequence → Dry and sanitize according to procedure → Put on new gloves if the task requires them.
options: Stop contact with the product and discard the soiled gloves
Dry and sanitize according to procedure
Put on new gloves if the task requires them
Wash your hands in the posted sequence
checks.prompt: In the workflow “Handwashing and glove replacement,” what should you do after completing the first step?

dialogue.japanese: 手袋を交換します。先に手を洗います。
dialogue.meaning: I will change my gloves. I will wash my hands first.
dialogue.reading: てぶくろをこうかんします。さきにてをあらいます。

dialogue.japanese: その手袋で食品に触らないでください。
dialogue.meaning: Do not touch food with those gloves.
dialogue.reading: そのてぶくろでしょくひんにさわらないでください。

objectives: Melakukan cuci tangan pada saat yang ditetapkan dan mengganti sarung tangan yang terkontaminasi.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Do not continue filling. Remove the gloves, wash your hands as required, and put on new gloves before handling the product again.
lessons.scenario: A worker touches a waste-bin handle with gloves and then prepares to fill a container with ready-to-eat product.

sections.body: Hands can transfer dirt or microorganisms from toilets, waste, money, raw ingredients, phones, and surfaces to food. Disposable gloves can also become contaminated and do not replace handwashing. The facility's plan specifies the washing, drying, and sanitizing steps and when gloves must be changed.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Wash your hands before starting, after using the toilet, after touching raw ingredients or waste, and when moving from a dirty task to a clean one. Remove gloves without touching food, discard them as required, wash your hands, and put on a new pair. Complete any required records.

Practice scenario: A worker touches a waste-bin handle with gloves and then prepares to fill a container with ready-to-eat product.
Suggested response: Do not continue filling. Remove the gloves, wash your hands as required, and put on new gloves before handling the product again.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Hentikan kontak dengan produk dan buang sarung tangan yang kotor
Cuci tangan sesuai urutan yang dipasang
Keringkan dan lakukan sanitasi sesuai prosedur
Pakai sarung tangan baru bila tugas memerlukannya
lessons.title: Handwashing and Glove Changes

lessons.caution: Do not assume equipment is ready to use just because its surface looks dry.

checks.explanation: Dirty equipment must not return to the clean workflow until it has gone through the facility's required steps.
options: Separate it, clean it, then sanitize it according to procedure
Wipe it quickly and put it on the clean shelf
Mix it with clean equipment so it dries together
Spray chemicals over the food
checks.prompt: What is the general sequence for preparing dirty equipment for reuse?

checks.explanation: After falling on the floor, the container's cleanliness cannot be assumed; separate it and request reprocessing.
options: Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Set the container aside as not ready for use and request washing and sanitizing again according to facility rules.
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Move the product to another group to meet the target
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: A container labeled clean falls on the floor near the raw-material area, and a worker wants to reuse it immediately. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Identify zone boundaries and equipment-status labels → Take clean equipment from its designated place → Separate used equipment in the washing area → Report equipment or surfaces that may be contaminated.
options: Take clean equipment from its designated place
Identify zone boundaries and equipment-status labels
Separate used equipment in the washing area
Report equipment or surfaces that may be contaminated
checks.prompt: In the workflow “Equipment cleaning and zone separation,” what should you do after completing the first step?

dialogue.japanese: この容器は床に落ちました。洗浄をお願いします。
dialogue.meaning: This container fell on the floor. Please wash it.
dialogue.reading: このようきはゆかにおちました。せんじょうをおねがいします。

dialogue.japanese: 清潔な器具はこの棚に置きます。
dialogue.meaning: Clean tools are kept on this shelf.
dialogue.reading: せいけつなきぐはこのたなにおきます。

objectives: Menjaga meja, pisau, wadah, dan alat tetap sesuai status bersih atau belum dibersihkan.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Set the container aside as not ready for use and request washing and sanitizing again according to facility rules.
lessons.scenario: A container marked clean falls on the floor near the raw-ingredient area, and a worker wants to reuse it immediately.

sections.body: Cleaning removes food residue and soil; sanitize according to procedure after the required cleaning steps. Equipment that looks clean is not necessarily ready to use. Facility markers, storage locations, and schedules show equipment status and boundaries between raw-material, processing, and ready-to-eat areas.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before starting, check equipment status labels and condition. After a dirty task, send tools to the correct wash area; do not put them back on the clean-equipment shelf. If a clean container falls or is splashed from a dirty area, set it aside and request a reassessment. Keep cleaning chemicals separate from food.

Practice scenario: A container marked clean falls on the floor near the raw-ingredient area, and a worker wants to reuse it immediately.
Suggested response: Set the container aside as not ready for use and request washing and sanitizing again according to facility rules.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Kenali batas zona dan label status alat
Ambil alat bersih dari tempat yang ditetapkan
Pisahkan alat bekas ke tempat pencucian
Laporkan alat atau permukaan yang terkena cemaran

modules.title: Worker Hygiene and Contamination Prevention

modules.description: Check material identity, condition, quantity, storage, and flow so lots and recipes remain matched throughout processing.

lessons.caution: Do not use ingredients with missing identity or conditions outside the criteria without approval.

checks.explanation: Lot numbers help trace ingredients when a discrepancy or product problem occurs.
options: Link ingredients to their supplier and the products made
Replace package-condition checks
Make all ingredients usable without restriction
Remove the need for process records
checks.prompt: What is the benefit of recording the lot number when ingredients are received?

checks.explanation: A mismatched lot or package must be separated and recorded before use.
options: Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Set the problem box aside, record its quantity and visible lot number, and ask the person in charge to decide whether to accept it.
Move the product to another group to meet the target
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: The documents list 12 boxes of ingredients, but one box is leaking and its lot number differs from the receiving list. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Match the documents and lot identity → Check the quantity, package, date, and required conditions → Record the inspection result and actual discrepancy → Hold any problem ingredients and request a decision.
options: Match the documents and lot identity
Check the quantity, package, date, and required conditions
Record the inspection result and actual discrepancy
Hold any problem ingredients and request a decision
checks.prompt: In the workflow “Inspecting incoming ingredients,” what should you do after completing the first step?

dialogue.japanese: ロット番号が書類と違います。確認してください。
dialogue.meaning: The lot number differs from the documents. Please check it.
dialogue.reading: ろっとばんごうがしょるいとちがいます。かくにんしてください。

dialogue.japanese: この箱は分けて、責任者に報告します。
dialogue.meaning: I am setting this box aside and reporting it to the person in charge.
dialogue.reading: このはこはわけて、せきにんしゃにほうこくします。

objectives: Mencocokkan nama bahan, nomor lot, jumlah, tanggal, kemasan, dan kondisi penerimaan dengan dokumen kerja.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Set the problem box aside, record the quantity and visible lot number, and ask the person in charge to decide whether to accept it.
lessons.scenario: The documents list 12 ingredient boxes, but one box is leaking and its lot number differs from the receiving list.

sections.body: Receiving links suppliers, ingredients, and lots to the finished product. Check documents against package markings, seal condition, leaks, damage, and temperature when required for the material. Acceptance criteria come from ingredient specifications and facility plans; hold nonconforming items for a decision by the person in charge.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use the designated measuring tools and record actual results, time, and lot number. Separate damaged packages or ingredients with mismatched records in the hold area without guessing whether they are acceptable. Do not change document figures or move a label from another lot.

Practice scenario: The documents list 12 ingredient boxes, but one box is leaking and its lot number differs from the receiving list.
Suggested response: Set the problem box aside, record the quantity and visible lot number, and ask the person in charge to decide whether to accept it.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Cocokkan dokumen dan identitas lot
Periksa jumlah, kemasan, tanggal, dan syarat kondisi
Catat hasil pemeriksaan dan selisih aktual
Tahan bahan bermasalah serta minta keputusan
lessons.title: Incoming Material Checks

lessons.caution: Do not rely on a remembered temperature instead of the limit specified for the product and process.

checks.explanation: Temperature requirements vary by ingredient and process; use the specified limit and record the result.
options: From the label or specification and the facility control plan
From an estimate based on the outdoor weather
From one value used for all foods
From the remaining quantity of ingredients
checks.prompt: Where should workers find the temperature limit for a particular ingredient?

checks.explanation: Record and hold deviations for the person in charge to decide; do not silently alter them.
options: Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Move the product to another group to meet the target
Hold the affected lot, record the time and reading, and report it so the person in charge can decide how to handle it.
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: The cold-room record shows a temperature above the limit on the form, but a lot is about to be used. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Read the storage requirements on the specification or label → Place the lot in the correctly identified location → Measure and record the temperature on the facility schedule → Hold and report deviations before using the ingredient.
options: Read the storage requirements on the specification or label
Measure and record the temperature on the facility schedule
Place the lot in the correctly identified location
Hold and report deviations before using the ingredient

dialogue.japanese: 表示の保存条件を確認します。
dialogue.meaning: I will check the storage conditions on the label.
dialogue.reading: ひょうじのほぞんじょうけんをかくにんします。

dialogue.japanese: 温度が基準を超えています。ロットを保留します。
dialogue.meaning: The temperature exceeded the limit. I am holding this lot.
dialogue.reading: おんどがきじゅんをこえています。ろっとをほりゅうします。

objectives: Menempatkan bahan pada lokasi dan kondisi simpan yang ditetapkan serta mencatat suhu sesuai rencana.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Hold the affected lot, record the time and reading, and report it so the person in charge can determine how to handle it.
lessons.scenario: Cold-room records show a temperature above the form's operating limit, but a lot is about to be used.

sections.body: Each ingredient has storage requirements set by the product, specification, and facility control system. Monitor refrigerator and freezer temperatures with the specified instruments and written limits; there is no single value that applies to every product. Separate raw ingredients from ready-to-eat products to prevent drips or contact.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Check storage labels, use marked shelves and containers, and record instrument readings at designated times. If temperature exceeds a limit, a door has been left open, or an instrument is questionable, hold the lot and report it. Do not change settings or decide on your own that the ingredients are still safe.

Practice scenario: Cold-room records show a temperature above the form's operating limit, but a lot is about to be used.
Suggested response: Hold the affected lot, record the time and reading, and report it so the person in charge can determine how to handle it.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Baca syarat simpan pada spesifikasi atau label
Tempatkan lot di lokasi beridentitas yang benar
Ukur dan catat suhu sesuai jadwal fasilitas
Tahan serta laporkan penyimpangan sebelum bahan dipakai
lessons.title: Storage and Temperature Monitoring

lessons.caution: Do not estimate quantities or substitute ingredients without recipe approval.

checks.explanation: Checking before weighing prevents the wrong ingredient from entering the mixture and preserves traceability.
options: So the mixture matches the formula and ingredients remain traceable
So the scale does not need to be checked
So the formula sequence can be changed freely
So actual records are unnecessary
checks.prompt: Why should the ingredient name and lot be checked before weighing a recipe?

checks.explanation: A mismatched label means the identity is uncertain; stop weighing until it is confirmed.
options: Do not start mixing. Set the container aside, compare its identity with the ingredient list, and ask the person in charge to confirm.
Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Move the product to another group to meet the target
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: The formula sheet calls for ingredient A powder, but the container on the table is labeled ingredient B and weighing has not begun. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Match the formula, ingredients, and lot → Check the units and scale condition → Weigh and record each ingredient separately → Add ingredients in sequence and mark the work completed.
options: Match the formula, ingredients, and lot
Weigh and record each ingredient separately
Add ingredients in sequence and mark the work completed
Check the units and scale condition

dialogue.japanese: 材料名とロット番号を照合します。
dialogue.meaning: I will match the ingredient name and lot number.
dialogue.reading: ざいりょうめいとろっとばんごうをしょうごうします。

dialogue.japanese: 表示が違うので、計量を止めます。
dialogue.meaning: The label is different, so I am stopping the weighing.
dialogue.reading: ひょうじがちがうので、けいりょうをとめます。

objectives: Menimbang bahan dengan satuan resep yang benar dan menjaga urutan penambahan serta identitas kelompok campuran.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Do not start mixing. Set the container aside, match its identity to the ingredient list, and ask the person in charge to confirm.
lessons.scenario: The recipe calls for ingredient A powder, but the container on the table is labeled ingredient B, and weighing has not started.

sections.body: The production recipe controls composition, yield, quality, and allergen information. Use scales suited to the required units, account for container tare, and add ingredients in the specified order. Line workers may not change a recipe or substitute ingredients unless an authorized person approves and records the change.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before opening a package, match the ingredient name and lot to the recipe sheet. Weigh one ingredient at a time, record the actual value, and mark each completed step. If a number, label, or quantity does not match, stop mixing and request a second check; do not substitute a nearby stock item.

Practice scenario: The recipe calls for ingredient A powder, but the container on the table is labeled ingredient B, and weighing has not started.
Suggested response: Do not start mixing. Set the container aside, match its identity to the ingredient list, and ask the person in charge to confirm.

steps: Cocokkan formula, bahan, dan lot
Periksa satuan serta kondisi timbangan
Timbang dan catat tiap bahan secara terpisah
Tambahkan menurut urutan dan tandai hasil kerja

modules.title: Receiving and Preparing Ingredients

modules.description: Follow process sequences, control limits, machine safeguards, and product changeovers, with attention to deviations and allergens.

lessons.caution: Do not open a guard or put your hand into a machine that has not been isolated according to procedure.

checks.explanation: Pre-operation checks find hazardous conditions before equipment moves and products enter the process.
options: Reduce the risk of entanglement, crushing, or contamination by loose objects
Allow the machine to run without a work checklist
Replace operator training
So minor damage does not need to be reported
checks.prompt: Why do workers check machine guards and the surrounding area before starting?

checks.explanation: A loose guard is unsafe; do not run the machine and escalate the issue for inspection.
options: Put on gloves and continue packaging as usual
Do not start the mixer. Keep people away from the hazard and tell the supervisor so the machine can be inspected.
Continue using estimated figures or ingredients without reporting it
Move the product to another group to meet the target
checks.prompt: Workplace scenario: A mixer guard feels loose, but the line is trying to meet its production target. The most appropriate action is to…

checks.explanation: The taught sequence is: Read the instructions and limits of the operator's role → Check guards, buttons, cables, and the surrounding area → Report damage or abnormal conditions → Start only after the machine is declared ready.
options: Check guards, buttons, cables, and the surrounding area
Read the instructions and limits of the operator's role
Report damage or abnormal conditions
Start only after the machine is declared ready

dialogue.japanese: 安全カバーがゆるんでいます。機械を止めます。
dialogue.meaning: The safety guard is loose. I am stopping the machine.
dialogue.reading: あんぜんかばーがゆるんでいます。きかいをとめます。

dialogue.japanese: 修理の人に確認してもらいます。
dialogue.meaning: I will ask maintenance staff to inspect it.
dialogue.reading: しゅうりのひとにかくにんしてもらいます。

objectives: Memeriksa kondisi mesin, tombol berhenti, pelindung, dan area kerja sebelum menjalankan alat yang menjadi tugasnya.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.
Menggunakan ungkapan Jepang sederhana untuk meminta konfirmasi atau melaporkan keadaan.
lessons.response: Do not start the mixer. Keep people away from the danger area and tell the leader so the machine can be inspected.
lessons.scenario: A mixer guard feels loose, but the line is trying to meet its production target.

sections.body: Food-processing machines such as mixers, cutters, and conveyors can trap or injure workers. Before work, check guards, emergency stops, cables, and the area for loose tools. Only instructed workers may operate or clean equipment; energy isolation and repairs follow local procedures and authorization.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Compare the machine with the startup checklist. Do not run it if a guard is loose, there is unusual noise or vibration, or a control cannot be tested as instructed. Post a sign if required and call the person in charge or a technician. Never put your hand near moving parts to clear a blockage.

Practice scenario: A mixer guard feels loose, but the line is trying to meet its production target.
Suggested response: Do not start the mixer. Keep people away from the danger area and tell the leader so the machine can be inspected.
sections.title: Applying the Procedures at Work

steps: Baca instruksi dan batas tugas operator
Periksa pelindung, tombol, kabel, dan area sekitar
Laporkan kerusakan atau keadaan tidak normal
Jalankan hanya setelah dinyatakan siap
lessons.title: Pre-Operation Machine and Guard Checks

options: Match the product with the process-control instructions

objectives: Membaca batas proses yang berlaku, memantau waktu atau suhu, dan menahan produk ketika kendali menyimpang.
Memilih tindakan aman pada satu situasi kerja dan menjelaskan alasannya.

lessons.response: Stop lot release, hold affected products, record the reading and time, and ask the person in charge to decide what to do.
lessons.scenario: Heating records show a reading below the limit in the product instructions, but the next trays are waiting.

sections.body: Heating, cooling, mixing, and other processes have parameters set for specific products. Check the lot instructions, use required instruments, and record actual results at monitoring points. If a reading is outside limits or an instrument fails, product made since the last check may need to be held for assessment.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before processing, verify that the product code, settings, and measuring instruments match the instructions. Record the start time, readings, and lot identity without rounding to hide a discrepancy. When an alarm sounds or a limit is exceeded, stop the line as instructed, mark affected product, and report it immediately.

Practice scenario: Heating records show a reading below the limit in the product instructions, but the next trays are waiting.
Suggested response: Stop lot release, hold affected products, record the reading and time, and ask the person in charge to decide what to do.

lessons.caution: Do not rely on memory or glove changes alone to declare a line free of allergens.

checks.explanation: Residues, ingredients, and labels must match the next product's specifications; hold product until this is verified.

Only the new package color
The quantity of product from the previous shift
An assumption that all ingredient residue is gone
checks.prompt: What must be verified before releasing product after an allergen changeover?

sections.body: Allergens can transfer through residue on machines, tables, gloves, measuring tools, or packaging. Allergen lists and label information may change under current requirements; use the product specifications and matrix in force at your facility. Production changeovers require approval, cleaning according to procedure, and another check of labels and lot identity.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
When changing to a product with a different allergen profile, hold startup until the changeover procedure is complete. Check designated equipment, new ingredients, and labels, and request a second check if required. If labels are mixed up or residue is visible, stop the line, separate product made since the last known-correct point, and report it. Do not promise an allergen-free product without official data.

Practice scenario: After a product containing milk, a label roll for a milk-free product is installed before the changeover cleaning record is complete.
Suggested response: Stop the line and hold product from the label change onward; report the sequence of events and wait for cleaning and label checks.

sections.body: Packaging protects food, and labels provide consumers with product identity and important information. Label rolls, packages, and products must therefore match the production plan. A wrong label can misstate product or allergen information even when the contents are correct. Check labels at startup, when packaging materials change, and at other points set by the facility.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Read the code on the work sheet and package, then compare it with the approved label sample. Check the print date, legibility, seal, and label orientation. If anything differs, stop packaging, hold product made since the last satisfactory check, record the code and quantity, and ask the person in charge to arrange a recheck.

Practice scenario: The label code on a new roll differs by one digit from the production sheet, and several packages have already been made.
Suggested response: Stop packaging, hold packages made since the last check, record the quantity and code, and report them for reinspection.

sections.body: Visual checks and designated inspection devices help detect damaged packaging, discoloration, missing parts, or foreign objects. Acceptance criteria vary by product. Follow standard samples and facility limits; do not decide on your own that a defect is safe. Do not bypass or adjust inspection devices without authorization.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
If you find a foreign object or an inspection-device alarm occurs, stop the line as instructed and use an identified hold container. Record the time, machine, product, lot, and quantity since the last accepted check. Do not discard evidence or put the same product back into the line before assessment.

Practice scenario: A worker sees a plastic fragment near a product on the conveyor and does not know whether it came from the packaging.
Suggested response: Stop or hold the line as instructed, separate the affected products, and report where and when the item was found for inspection.

sections.body: Production records link ingredients, parameters, inspections, packaging, and lot results. Record actual facts, times, product identity, and actions taken. At shift change, communicate the status of held items, faulty machines, and unfinished checks verbally and in writing according to the facility's system.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Complete forms as work is performed rather than from memory at shift end. Do not erase an incorrect value; use the official correction method so the change remains visible. During handover, state the lot number, hold location and reason, checks already completed, and who must follow up. Ask the recipient to repeat key points if anything is unclear.

Practice scenario: At shift end, a lot is still awaiting a label check, but the next worker receives only the production quantity record.
Suggested response: Record the lot status, hold location, reason, and outstanding check according to correction rules, then hand it over directly to the next shift.
